1:1.t: "In Ephesus": the KJV's reading; some early manuscripts do not have these words, and the letter may have been meant for several churches in the province of Asia.

2:14.t: "The dividing wall": perhaps recalling the barrier in the temple that kept Gentiles out of the inner courts (see Acts 21:28).

3:9.t: "The fellowship of this mystery": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "the administration of this mystery". "Through Jesus Christ": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts do not have these words.

3:14.t: "Of our Lord Jesus Christ": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts do not have these words.

4:8.t: A quotation of Psalm 68:18, where God receives gifts; Paul follows a Jewish reading in which He gives them.

4:9.t: "First": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts do not have this word. "The lower parts of the earth": either the earth itself (the incarnation) or the realm of the dead.

4:26.t: "In your anger do not sin" (Greek orgizesthe kai me hamartanete): the KJV's "Be ye angry, and sin not". Anger itself is not forbidden; letting it lead to sin, or nursing it, is.

5:9.t: "The fruit of the Spirit": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "the fruit of the light".

5:14.t: Perhaps from an early Christian hymn, echoing Isaiah 60:1.

5:30.t: "Of His flesh and of His bones": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts do not have these words.

6:2.t: A quotation of Exodus 20:12 and Deuteronomy 5:16.

6:5.t: Paul addresses slavery as it existed in the Roman world. He does not endorse it as an institution; he puts master and slave under one Master who shows no favoritism (6:9). Compare 1 Corinthians 7:21 and Philemon 16.

6:24.t: "With an undying love": the KJV's "in sincerity"; Greek en aphtharsia, "in incorruption".

1:3.t: "The heavenly realms" (Greek en tois epouraniois): the KJV's "heavenly places", a phrase used five times in Ephesians for the unseen spiritual world where Christ reigns and where spiritual conflict takes place (1:20, 2:6, 3:10, 6:12).

1:4.t: "Chose ... predestined" (Greek exelexato ... proorisas): Christians have understood God's foreknowledge and predestination differently: as God's choosing of His people beforehand, or as His knowing beforehand who would believe (see Romans 8:29-30). Paul stresses that God's choosing is "in Him", in Christ, and "in love".

1:10.t: "Bring unity to all things ... under Christ" (Greek anakephalaiosasthai): to sum up, gather together under one head. "Administration" (Greek oikonomia): the KJV's "dispensation", a household management, God's plan for the ages.

1:13.t: "Seal ... deposit": the KJV's "sealed ... earnest". A seal marked ownership; a deposit (Greek arrabon) was a first installment guaranteeing full payment. The Spirit is God's guarantee of the salvation to come. See 2 Corinthians 1:22.

1:23.t: "Fullness" (Greek pleroma): the church is filled by Christ, and in some sense completes Him as a body completes its head.

2:8.t: "By grace ... through faith ... not from yourselves": the source of salvation is God's grace; the means of receiving it is faith. "This" (Greek touto) is neuter and refers to the whole of salvation, not faith alone.

2:10.t: "Handiwork" (Greek poiema): the KJV's "workmanship", the source of "poem". Believers are God's masterpiece, created for good works.

2:15.t: "One new humanity" (Greek hena kainon anthropon): the KJV's "one new man", Jews and Gentiles made one people in Christ.

3:6.t: "Mystery" (Greek mysterion): not a puzzle but a secret once hidden and now revealed by God; see Matthew 13:11. Here it is God's long-hidden plan to include the Gentiles fully with Israel in one body.

3:15.t: "Every family ... derives its name" (Greek pasa patria ... onomazetai): a wordplay: patria, family, comes from pater, father. All fatherhood takes its name from God the Father.

3:19.t: "This love that surpasses knowledge": the love of Christ (agape) can be known by experience, yet never fully grasped.

4:11.t: "Pastors" (Greek poimenas): literally "shepherds". "Pastors and teachers" may describe one role.

4:12.t: "To equip" (Greek katartismos): the KJV's "perfecting", to mend, restore, fit out. Leaders equip all believers for ministry.

4:30.t: "Grieve" (Greek lypeite): the Spirit is a person who can be grieved, not merely a force.

5:18.t: "Be filled with the Spirit" (Greek plerousthe en pneumati): a present command, "keep being filled".

5:21.t: "Submit" (Greek hypotasso): verse 22 has no verb in the Greek; it borrows "submit" from verse 21, which calls all believers to mutual submission. Christians differ on how the husband's headship and the wife's submission (5:22-33) apply today; all agree that the husband's model is Christ's self-giving love (5:25).

5:32.t: "Mystery" (Greek mysterion): not a puzzle but a secret once hidden and now revealed by God; see 3:6. The Latin Bible translated it sacramentum, which contributed to the later teaching that marriage is a sacrament.

6:11.t: "Armor" (Greek panoplia): the full equipment of a Roman heavy infantryman. Paul draws on Isaiah 11:5, 52:7 and 59:17, where God Himself wears the armor.

6:12.t: "Rulers ... authorities ... powers" (Greek archai, exousiai, kosmokratores): spiritual powers of evil. See 1:21 and 3:10.
